| `profile_embedding_loss_sidecar_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node2Vec-like algorithms return loss history, THEN loss vector length, numeric type, bytes, iteration mapping, and configuration echo SHALL be recorded separately from the embedding matrix. |
| `profile_embedding_algorithm_label_caveat_v1` | WHEN procedure/progress labels are recorded, THEN public procedure name, source-level algorithm label, result-builder type, and any mismatch caveat SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_ml_topk_relationship_receipt_v1` | WHEN KGE or similar ML top-k output runs, THEN source filter, target filter, topK, candidate-pair estimate, score function, embedding property, relationship-type embedding, and queue bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_kge_stream_fixture_oracle_v1` | WHEN KGE stream parity is verified, THEN source/target filters, topK, score function, expected rows, score tolerance, and original-id mapping SHALL be pinned. |
| `profile_kge_write_target_receipt_v1` | WHEN KGE write mode runs, THEN `TopKGraph` relationship count, write relationship type, score property, exporter target, result-store flag, job id, and write timings SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_kge_mutate_graph_store_receipt_v1` | WHEN KGE mutate mode runs, THEN relationship builder orientation, aggregation, property key, concurrency, graph-store relationship type, relationships written, and graph equality SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_model_provenance_sidecar_receipt_v1` | WHEN a pipeline-backed ML prediction is attempted, THEN model name, username, model catalog id, train config hash, pipeline hash, classifier type, graph-store filter, and dependency context SHALL be recorded. |

#### Embedding Memory Estimates Make The Matrix Story Honest

Pass 107 corrects the easy overstatement from pass 106.

The phrase "embedding matrix output" is directionally right for the public
artifact, but it is not enough for a RAM cap. Each embedding algorithm carries
its own resident and temporary state before the public matrix exists.

The better model is:

```text
embedding_profile_v1:
  durable_output_carrier
  algorithm_scratch_state
  training_or_inference_state
  public_api_materializer
  side_effect_target
  estimate_receipt
  measured_peak_receipt
```

FastRP is the simple warning:

```text
FastRP estimate:
  property_vectors:
    feature_property_count * property_dimension
  per_node_embeddings:
    embeddings
    embeddingsA
    embeddingsB
```

So even a predictable FastRP output should be described as matrix plus work
matrices, not as one matrix. The GDS fixture makes this concrete: a 128-wide
FastRP profile reaches about 1.596 GB estimated memory at 1,000,000 nodes in
the tested configuration, and the estimate was unchanged across the tested
concurrency values. The exact number is a GDS fixture value, not a universal
benchmark; the product lesson is that the receipt can be deterministic enough
to compare against our own implementation.

Node2Vec is a different shape:

```text
Node2Vec estimate:
  random_walks:
    node_count * walks_per_node * walk_length * long_width
  probability_cache:
    node_frequencies
    positive_sampling_probabilities
    negative_sampling_distribution
  model:
    center_embeddings
    context_embeddings
  public_output:
    final embedding matrix
```

This means Node2Vec cannot share a FastRP RAM promise just because both return
embeddings. A budget-bounded Node2Vec mode needs an explicit walk-store policy:
in-memory, chunked, mmap, spill, generated-on-demand, or refused under cap.

GraphSAGE splits even harder:

```text
GraphSAGE inference/mutate:
  initial_features
  concurrent_batches
  result_features:
    resident in mutate mode
    temporary in non-mutate mode

GraphSAGE training:
  resident weights
  optimizer state
  multilabel weight ranges
  train-on-epoch temporary state
  per-thread expanded batches
  forward aggregators
  backward aggregators
```

The practical implication: GraphSAGE is not one algorithm SKU. It is at least:

```text
graphsage_inference_stream_profile
graphsage_inference_mutate_profile
graphsage_train_mean_aggregator_profile
graphsage_train_pool_aggregator_profile
```

Aggregator choice matters. The source estimate makes mean aggregation a smaller
buffer profile, while pool aggregation carries materially more embedding-width
buffers. For Knight Bus, that means aggregator type, fanout, batch size, layer
dimensions, and gradient-descent flag must be visible in the planner before a
run starts.

HashGNN is the most product-relevant precedent:

```text
HashGNN estimate:
  compact internal state:
    HugeAtomicBitSet embedding caches
    hashes cache
  public materialization:
    dense output range
```

That is almost exactly the storage doctrine:

```text
Store compact in the shape of compute.
Materialize dense in the shape of Neo4j/GDS API.
Expose the sparse-min to dense-max range before execution.
```

KGE then needs a caveat. Runtime source shows source and target bitsets plus
`TopKMapComputer`, but the searched code graph did not expose an obvious
dedicated KGE memory-estimate definition. Separately, `TopKMap.memoryEstimation`
traces clearly into node similarity. So the safest conclusion is:

```text
KGE should borrow top-k accounting,
but must add KGE-specific candidate and scorer receipts.
```

The Knight Bus KGE estimate should include:

```text
kge_estimate_receipt_v1:
  source_filter_bitset_bytes
  target_filter_bitset_bytes
  source_cardinality
  target_cardinality
  candidate_pair_upper_bound
  existing_link_exclusion_policy
  embedding_property_ref
  relationship_type_embedding_ref
  scorer_function
  scorer_input_bytes
  topk_queue_bytes
  output_pair_count
  stream_write_mutate_materializer_bytes
  searched_source_caveat
```

Rubber duck check:

```text
If we count only the final embedding matrix:
  FastRP, Node2Vec, and GraphSAGE are under-estimated.

If training and inference share a profile:
  GraphSAGE caps will lie because batch, optimizer, and backward-pass state are
  not present in inference.

If KGE simply reuses the KNN bundle:
  source/target filters, scorer inputs, relationship-type embeddings, and
  existing-link exclusion disappear from the estimate.

If compact sparse output is materialized eagerly:
  the cap can still be broken at the API boundary even if compute stayed small.
```

The pass-107 product decision:

```text
Embedding outputs remain a strong early lane,
but each algorithm needs a memory-profile subtype:

FastRP:
  matrix plus A/B scratch matrices

Node2Vec:
  walk store plus probability cache plus model matrices

GraphSAGE inference:
  feature and batch state plus mode-specific result residency

GraphSAGE training:
  weights plus optimizer plus expanded sampled batches

HashGNN:
  compact bitset state plus dense materialization range

KGE:
  top-k edge-score output plus KGE-specific candidate/scorer admission
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_fastrp_three_matrix_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN FastRP is estimated, THEN output embedding bytes, A/B work-matrix bytes, property-vector bytes, node count, dimension, concurrency, fixture expectation, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_node2vec_walk_model_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node2Vec is estimated, THEN walks-per-node, walk length, random-walk bytes, probability-cache bytes, center/context embedding bytes, loss sidecar, fixture expectation, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_graphsage_resident_temporary_split_receipt_v1` | WHEN GraphSAGE inference/export/mutate is estimated, THEN mode, result residency category, feature bytes, result bytes, batch bytes, concurrency, and resident-vs-temporary peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_graphsage_training_batch_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN GraphSAGE training is estimated, THEN weights, optimizer state, multilabel ranges, fanout-expanded batch ranges, forward/backward bytes, and min/max memory SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_graphsage_aggregator_cost_selector_v1` | WHEN GraphSAGE chooses an aggregator, THEN mean/pool identity, input dimension, embedding dimension, previous/current node counts, buffer formula, and selected memory range SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_hashgnn_sparse_dense_range_receipt_v1` | WHEN HashGNN is estimated, THEN bitset-cache bytes, hashes-cache bytes, binary dimension, output dimension, sparse-min bytes, dense-max bytes, and materialization policy SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_kge_candidate_topk_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN KGE prediction is estimated, THEN source/target filter bytes, candidate-pair upper bound, scorer inputs, topK queue bytes, output count, and stream/write/mutate materializer bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_embedding_estimate_fixture_matrix_v1` | WHEN an embedding estimate is ported from GDS fixtures, THEN source fixture path, exact config, expected bytes, our estimated bytes, measured peak, and delta SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_topk_estimate_wiring_caveat_v1` | WHEN top-k estimation is reused across algorithms, THEN the source path that directly wires the estimate and any missing algorithm-specific estimate path SHALL be recorded. |

#### Starter Slice Estimates Are The First Verification Spine

Pass 108 turns the starter slice into a sharper verification plan.

The first deliverable should not be "we run WCC/PageRank/BFS." It should be:

```text
For each starter algorithm:
  1. estimate memory before execution
  2. explain the estimate as named components
  3. compare estimate against cap
  4. either refuse or run
  5. measure peak bytes
  6. compare output against GDS fixture
  7. save the full receipt
```

That is more product-defining than a raw algorithm port because it gives the
user a budget contract before the run begins.

WCC is the first exact estimate port:

```text
WCC estimate:
  dss:
    HugeAtomicDisjointSetStruct.memoryEstimation(isIncremental)

fixture facts:
  non_incremental:
    0 nodes -> 64 bytes
    100 nodes -> 864 bytes
    100,000,000,000 nodes -> 800,122,070,392 bytes

  incremental:
    0 nodes -> 104 bytes
    100 nodes -> 1,704 bytes
    100,000,000,000 nodes -> 1,600,244,140,760 bytes

  concurrency:
    100-node estimate unchanged at concurrency 1, 4, and 128
```

Product interpretation:

```text
WCC is a perfect first receipt because the state is one named component:
  component ids / disjoint-set structure

The low-RAM innovation can be explored later:
  compressed parents
  union-log plus checkpoints
  mmap parent table
  shard-local parents plus merge passes

But v1 should first prove exact byte parity against the GDS-style estimate.
```

PageRank is the first iterative/Pregel receipt:

```text
PageRank estimate:
  Pregel.memoryEstimation(
    propertiesMap = { "pagerank": DOUBLE },
    isQueueBased = false,
    isAsync = false,
    isTrackingSender = false
  )

Pregel components:
  vote bits
  per-thread compute steps
  node value:
    pagerank DOUBLE -> HugeDoubleArray(node_count)
  message arrays:
    send array -> HugeAtomicDoubleArray(node_count)
    receive array -> HugeAtomicDoubleArray(node_count)
```

The PageRank fixture makes concurrency visible:

```text
100,000 nodes
1,000,000 relationships

concurrency 1  -> 2,412,832 bytes
concurrency 4  -> 2,413,000 bytes
concurrency 42 -> 2,415,128 bytes

10,000,000,000 nodes
10,000,000,000 relationships
concurrency 4 -> 241,286,621,640 bytes
```

Product interpretation:

```text
PageRank is not mainly an io_uring story.
PageRank is a state-layout and message-reduction story.

Rust helps if it lets us:
  store values in tighter typed arrays
  choose exact reduced-width counters where safe
  stream partitions with bounded message buffers
  avoid boxed/runtime overhead at the API boundary
  prove convergence fields and numeric tolerances

Rust alone does not remove the mathematical need for rank values,
message/reduction state, and convergence bookkeeping.
```

BFS is the first cap-vs-latency receipt:

```text
BFS fixed/global state:
  visited
  traversedNodes
  weights
  minimumChunk
  resultNodes

BFS variable/frontier state:
  localNodes lower bound:
    node_count + node_count / 64

  localNodes upper bound:
    min(
      relationship_count_upper_bound,
      concurrency * (node_count - 1)
    ) + node_count / 64

  chunks:
    node_count / 64
```

The BFS fixture makes the tradeoff legible:

```text
10,000 nodes / 100,000 relationships:
  concurrency 1 -> 402,988..402,988 bytes
  concurrency 2 -> 402,988..482,972 bytes

100,000 nodes / 1,000,000 relationships:
  concurrency 1 -> 4,026,890..4,026,890 bytes
  concurrency 2 -> 4,026,890..4,826,874 bytes
```

Product interpretation:

```text
BFS is the first place where Knight Bus can show a clear knob:

  "Use less RAM by reducing or bounding local frontier buffers.
   Spend more time by draining/synchronizing/spilling earlier."

The cap policy can be explicit:
  ram_first:
    larger local frontier buffers
    higher concurrency
    lower latency

  bounded_ram:
    smaller local frontier buffers
    lower concurrency
    chunked frontier drains
    optional mmap/spill
    predictable peak bytes
```

The public estimate endpoint is itself a product surface.

GDS exposes estimate procedures that return data like:

```text
requiredMemory
treeView
mapView
bytesMin
bytesMax
nodeCount
relationshipCount
heapPercentageMin
heapPercentageMax
```

Knight Bus should extend that with storage-profile identity:

```text
estimate_endpoint_v1:
  algorithm
  mode
  graph_or_fictitious_dimensions
  config
  selected_storage_profile
  exactness_mode
  bytes_min
  bytes_max
  cap_bytes
  accepted_or_refused
  refusal_reason_optional
  component_tree
  component_map
  planned_latency_band_optional
```

This unlocks the workflow the product is really trying to sell:

```text
User:
  "Run PageRank, but never exceed 5 GB."

System:
  "Profile A fits at 4.3 GB, estimated 38 minutes.
   Profile B needs 12.1 GB, estimated 9 minutes.
   Profile C fits at 2.1 GB, estimated 2.4 hours.
   Choose one or let policy decide."
```

Rubber duck check:

```text
If WCC is not estimate-compatible first:
  the simplest scalar-vector proof is still not trustworthy.

If PageRank is described as "Rust will be faster":
  the actual Pregel state model disappears, and the claim becomes vibes.

If BFS does not separate fixed arrays from frontier ranges:
  the most obvious RAM/latency knob is hidden.

If estimate endpoints are skipped:
  budget-bounded compute becomes an internal benchmark instead of a product
  promise a user can rely on.
```

The pass-108 product decision:

```text
Build the first executable verification spine in this order:

1. WCC estimate receipt:
   exact DSS bytes, incremental flag, fixture parity

2. WCC output receipt:
   partition equivalence, stream/stats/write/mutate API rows

3. PageRank estimate receipt:
   Pregel value/message/vote bits, concurrency fixture parity

4. PageRank output receipt:
   score tolerance, convergence fields, stream/stats/write/mutate rows

5. BFS estimate receipt:
   fixed arrays, frontier range, concurrency/cap tradeoff

6. BFS output receipt:
   target/depth/direction/path materialization parity

Only after this should we sell KNN, embeddings, path bundles, or KGE as
product-quality RAM-saving modes.
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_wcc_dss_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN WCC is estimated, THEN incremental flag, node count, concurrency, DSS component bytes, expected fixture bytes, bytesMin/bytesMax equality, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_public_estimate_row_receipt_v1` | WHEN any estimate endpoint runs, THEN `requiredMemory`, `treeView`, `mapView`, `bytesMin`, `bytesMax`, graph dimensions, heap percentages, one-row invariant, and selected storage profile SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pregel_double_value_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN a Pregel DOUBLE node-value algorithm is estimated, THEN property map, node-value array bytes, vote-bit bytes, per-thread compute-step bytes, concurrency, and expected fixture bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pagerank_pregel_message_receipt_v1` | WHEN PageRank is estimated, THEN queue-vs-array mode, async flag, sender-tracking flag, send-array bytes, receive-array bytes, relationship count, and expected fixture bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pagerank_estimate_fixture_receipt_v1` | WHEN PageRank estimate parity is tested, THEN GDS fixture config, concurrency, expected bytes, our estimated bytes, measured peak, and delta SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_global_array_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS is estimated, THEN visited, traversedNodes, weights, minimumChunk, resultNodes, and fixed global bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_frontier_range_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS frontier state is estimated, THEN localNodes lower formula, upper formula, chunk separator count, concurrency, relationship upper bound, expected min/max, and cap-policy decision SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_public_estimate_fixture_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS estimate parity is tested through the public API, THEN source node, target nodes, stats/stream mode, bytesMin, bytesMax, node count, relationship count, and selected storage profile SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_algorithm_estimate_endpoint_contract_v1` | WHEN a user asks whether an algorithm fits under a cap, THEN the system SHALL return accepted/refused status, selected profile, byte range, component tree, component map, and refusal reason before execution. |

#### KNN And Node Similarity Are Edge-Score Estimate Families

Pass 109 sharpens the next relationship-output slice after the WCC/PageRank/BFS
starter trio.

The important product point is that KNN and Node Similarity both produce
edge-score-like outputs, but their memory receipts are not the same.

```text
KNN estimate family:
  top-k-neighbors-list:
    one NeighborList per node
    each NeighborList stores 2 * k longs

  temporary neighbor lists:
    old-neighbors
    new-neighbors
    old-reverse-neighbors
    new-reverse-neighbors
    each is a HugeObjectArray range over node count

  sampler state:
    initial-random-neighbors per thread
    uniform sampler:
      LongUniformSamplerFromRange + sampler instance
    random-walk sampler:
      RandomWalkSampler(k * WALK_LENGTH_MULTIPLIER)
      sampler instance
      long array
      long hash set
      LongUniformSamplerFromRange min/max union

  sampled-random-neighbors:
    int-array hash container per thread
```

The source fixture is already useful as an executable port target:

```text
KNN fixture axes:
  node_count:
    1
    10
    100
    1000
    1,000,000,000
    100,000,000,000

  initial_sampler:
    UNIFORM
    RANDOMWALK

  formula:
    algorithm object
    + topK neighbor lists
    + 4 temporary neighbor arrays
    + initial sampler
    + sampled random list
```

Product interpretation:

```text
KNN is not "run nearest neighbors over graph in RAM."

It is:
  maintain bounded neighbor candidates
  keep old/new/reverse deltas
  pick a sampler shape
  spend iterations to improve quality
  eventually emit an edge-score bundle

So the first low-RAM KNN profiles should be named like this:

  knn_gds_compatible_profile:
    match GDS estimate formulas first

  knn_uniform_low_scratch_profile:
    prefer uniform sampler
    cap sampled lists
    accept more iterations / lower initial quality

  knn_randomwalk_quality_profile:
    spend sampler scratch for better graph-aware starts
    expose random-walk memory separately

  knn_spillable_temp_neighbor_profile:
    keep topK resident
    spill old/new/reverse temporary arrays by shard
```

Filtered KNN is a caveat. In the inspected GDS estimate definition, filtered KNN
adds the regular KNN estimate and does not add a separate filter-sidecar estimate.
For strict GDS parity, that is the receipt. For Knight Bus product claims, we
should not hide filter state if our profile materializes source/target filters.

Node Similarity has a different shape:

```text
Node Similarity estimate family:
  node filter:
    bitset over nodes

  vectors:
    HugeObjectArray of long arrays
    average degree derived from relationship upper bound / node count

  weights:
    HugeObjectArray of double arrays
    optional range from zero to full average-degree arrays

  component mode:
    nodes sorted by component
    upper bound per component
    WCC estimate when component ids must be computed
    component mapping when component property is provided

  output selection:
    TopKMap when topK is set
    TopNList when topN is set
    SimilarityGraphBuilder when computing to graph without topK
```

The source fixture makes the topK curve impossible to ignore:

```text
1,000,000 nodes
5,000,000 relationships

topK = 10:
  expected topK memory = 248,000,016 bytes

topK = 100:
  expected topK memory = 1,688,000,016 bytes
```

Rubber duck check:

```text
If we say "KNN and Node Similarity share storage":
  false enough to be dangerous.
  They can share an output edge-score bundle,
  but their compute-state receipts are different.

If we store the final similarity graph too early:
  we may pay graph-materialization bytes before the user needs a graph.

If we keep only topK queues:
  we may satisfy stream/topK workloads with far less resident memory,
  but write/mutate graph parity needs a materializer receipt.

If we treat topN as just another topK:
  wrong.
  topK is per-source bounded.
  topN is a global queue.
  Their memory and semantics differ.
```

The architecture decision from this pass:

```text
Relationship-output storage profiles should be selected by compute artifact:

1. per-node-topk-queue:
   best for Node Similarity topK and KNN candidate state
   low memory when k is small
   needs final bundle materializer

2. global-topn-queue:
   best for topN-style global result limits
   bounded by topN
   risks losing per-source fairness unless declared

3. edge-score-bundle:
   durable compact output:
     src[]
     dst[]
     score[]
     optional segment offsets
   good for stream/write/result-store

4. materialized-similarity-graph:
   Neo4j/GDS-compatible graph-shaped output
   useful for downstream graph algorithms
   should be explicit because adjacency-list bytes can dominate

5. spillable-candidate-state:
   shard old/new/reverse KNN temp lists
   keep resident topK and active shard only
   slower but cap-friendly
```

The pass-109 implementation sequence:

```text
After WCC/PageRank/BFS estimate parity:

1. Port KNN estimate formula:
   neighbor lists
   temp neighbor ranges
   sampler choices
   filtered-KNN parity caveat

2. Port Node Similarity estimate formula:
   node filter
   vector/weight arrays
   component/WCC options
   topK/topN/materialized graph options

3. Expose public estimate endpoints:
   gds-compatible mode
   bounded-ram mode
   selected storage profile
   bytesMin/bytesMax
   accepted/refused status

4. Only then implement output parity:
   stream edge-score rows
   stats counters
   write/mutate one-row summaries
   graph equality for written relationships
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_knn_neighbor_list_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN is estimated, THEN node count, k, neighbor-list element bytes, per-node topK list bytes, expected fixture bytes, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_temporary_neighbor_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN temporary state is estimated, THEN old/new/reverse temp-list lower and upper ranges, sampled k, concurrency, cap decision, and selected storage profile SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_sampler_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN sampler state is estimated, THEN sampler type, bounded k, random-walk multiplier, range sampler bytes, long-array bytes, hash-set bytes, per-thread multiplier, and quality/iteration caveat SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_filtered_knn_filter_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN filtered KNN is estimated, THEN GDS-compatible estimate bytes, filter inputs, any Knight Bus filter sidecar bytes, and a parity-vs-profile explanation SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_vector_weight_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity vector state is estimated, THEN node count, relationship upper bound, average degree, vector bytes, weight bytes, min/max range, and fixture delta SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_component_wcc_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity uses component pruning, THEN component-property flag, run-WCC flag, sorted-component bytes, upper-bound bytes, WCC/component-mapping bytes, and fixture delta SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_topk_topn_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity result limiting is estimated, THEN topK, topN, actual clamped values, per-node queue bytes, global queue bytes, and semantic tradeoff SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_similarity_graph_materializer_receipt_v1` | WHEN a similarity graph is materialized, THEN candidate-pair upper bound, topK/topN caps, new node count, new relationship count, average degree, adjacency-list bytes, and downstream-use reason SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_similarity_edge_score_estimate_endpoint_v1` | WHEN a similarity estimate endpoint is called, THEN public procedure name, mode, filter variant, parsed config, estimator class, selected storage profile, bytesMin, bytesMax, cap result, and output materializer SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_relationship_output_estimate_family_selector_v1` | WHEN an edge-score algorithm is planned, THEN the system SHALL choose per-node-topk, global-topn, edge-score-bundle, materialized-graph, or spillable-candidate-state before execution and record why. |

#### Similarity Output Fixtures Are The Next Verification Loop

Pass 110 turns KNN and Node Similarity from "interesting algorithms" into
concrete compatibility targets.

The core rewrite rule:

```text
Do not start with a giant graph benchmark.

Start with tiny fixture parity:
  run the GDS-style query
  assert exact rows/counters/side effects
  run our query
  assert the same rows/counters/side effects
  compare memory receipt
  only then scale up
```

KNN's output fixture is compact:

```text
KNN stream:
  graph:
    three nodes with `knn` property
  config:
    topK = 1
    randomSeed = 19
    concurrency = 1
  expected rows:
    a -> b, similarity 0.5
    b -> a, similarity 0.5
    c -> b, similarity 0.25

KNN label-filter stream:
  nodeLabels = ["Foo"]
  expected rows:
    dave -> bob, similarity 1.0
    bob -> dave, similarity 1.0
```

KNN's summary modes are also fixture-grade:

```text
KNN stats/write/mutate:
  one row
  nodesCompared = 3
  nodePairsConsidered = 37
  similarityPairs or relationshipsWritten = 3
  didConverge = true
  ranIterations = 1
  computeMillis >= 0
  preProcessingMillis >= 0
  writeMillis or mutateMillis >= 0 when applicable
  postProcessingMillis = 0 for write/mutate fixtures
  distribution keys:
    min max mean stdDev p1 p5 p10 p25 p50 p75 p90 p95 p99 p100
  config echo:
    writeRelationshipType / mutateRelationshipType
    writeProperty / mutateProperty
```

Write mode adds graph equality:

```text
KNN written graph:
  (a {id: 1})-[:SIMILAR {w: 0.5}]->(b {id: 2})
  (b)-[:SIMILAR {w: 0.5}]->(a)
  (c {id: 3})-[:SIMILAR {w: 0.25}]->(b)
```

The product implication is a clean edge-bundle oracle:

```text
src[]:
  a, b, c
dst[]:
  b, a, b
score[]:
  0.5, 0.5, 0.25

receipt:
  id map
  row order clause
  score tolerance
  distribution fields
  write/mutate target
  graph equality proof
```

Filtered KNN adds source/target filtering:

```text
filtered KNN:
  nodeLabels = ["Foo"]
  sourceNodeFilter = [dave]
    expected:
      dave -> bob, similarity 1.0

  targetNodeFilter = [bob]
    expected:
      dave -> bob, similarity 1.0

  write aliases:
    gds.alpha.knn.filtered
    gds.knn.filtered
```

This means compatibility has two layers:

```text
semantic layer:
  filters change which rows are emitted

API layer:
  legacy/current proc names must still map to the same behavior
```

Node Similarity is richer and should be its own fixture family:

```text
Node Similarity stream dimensions:
  projection orientation:
    outgoing
    incoming

  result controls:
    similarityCutoff
    topN
    degreeCutoff

  graph caveat:
    parallel edges are ignored for similarity result purposes

  metric caveat:
    cosine similarity config must be accepted
```

Expected stream scores include:

```text
outgoing:
  0 -> 1, 2/3
  0 -> 2, 1/3
  1 -> 2, 0
  mandatory topK reverse rows also appear

incoming:
  4 -> 5, 1.0
  4 -> 6, 1/3
  5 -> 6, 1/3
  mandatory topK reverse rows also appear
```

Node Similarity summary and write/mutate fixtures:

```text
stats:
  one row
  nodesCompared = 3
  similarityPairs = 6
  distribution keys present
  configuration present

write:
  relationshipsWritten = 6
  relationship type / score property echoed
  orientation-specific graph equality

mutate:
  relationshipsWritten = 6
  one row
  distribution keys present
  configuration present

unique relationship checks:
  topK = 1
  topN = 0 or 10
  relationshipsWritten = 6
```

Filtered Node Similarity exposes a useful compute-vs-output distinction:

```text
no filter:
  stream rows = 10
  nodesCompared = 4
  similarityPairs = 10
  relationshipsWritten = 10

source filter [a, d]:
  stream rows = 6
  nodesCompared = 2
  similarityPairs = 6
  relationshipsWritten = 6

target filter [a, d]:
  stream rows = 6
  nodesCompared = 4
  similarityPairs = 6
  relationshipsWritten = 6
```

This is an important architecture clue:

```text
source filter:
  lowers compute state
  can reduce vector scans
  can reduce topK queues

target filter:
  may keep source compute wide
  reduces emitted pairs
  can reduce output materialization

Therefore:
  source_filter_bytes
  target_filter_bytes
  compared_source_count
  emitted_pair_count
  written_relationship_count

should be separate receipt fields.
```

Rubber duck check:

```text
If the edge-score bundle matches rows but not write graph equality:
  it is not yet GDS-compatible.

If stats counters match but distribution keys are missing:
  dashboard/API parity is incomplete.

If filters are applied after full materialization:
  row parity may pass while RAM differentiation fails.

If source and target filters are not separated:
  the planner cannot explain why one reduces compute and the other reduces
  output.

If Node Similarity and KNN share only one test harness:
  topN, degree cutoff, orientation, and parallel-edge semantics will be missed.
```

The pass-110 implementation decision:

```text
Build similarity verification in this order:

1. KNN tiny stream fixture:
   exact rows and scores

2. KNN stats/write/mutate summary fixture:
   counters, convergence, distribution, config echo

3. KNN written graph equality:
   reproject SIMILAR relationships and compare topology/score

4. Filtered KNN:
   source/target filter rows and legacy/current procedure names

5. Node Similarity stream:
   orientation, topN, degree cutoff, duplicate edge behavior

6. Node Similarity summary/write/mutate:
   counters, graph equality, distribution, topK/topN interaction

7. Filtered Node Similarity:
   source-vs-target filter compute/output split

Only after these fixtures are green should we claim large-dataset RAM wins.
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_knn_output_fixture_parity_v1` | WHEN the tiny KNN stream fixture runs, THEN expected node1/node2/similarity rows, ordering rule, id mapping, score tolerance, and selected storage profile SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_stats_summary_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN stats runs, THEN nodesCompared, nodePairsConsidered, didConverge, ranIterations, similarityPairs, timing columns, configuration, and distribution keys SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_write_mutate_side_effect_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN write or mutate runs, THEN relationship count, relationship type, score property, side-effect target, timing columns, one-row invariant, and graph-store/native equality SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_filtered_knn_output_filter_parity_v1` | WHEN filtered KNN runs, THEN label filter, source filter, target filter, expected rows, compared nodes, emitted pairs, and filter sidecar bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_similarity_legacy_proc_alias_receipt_v1` | WHEN an alpha/current similarity procedure alias exists, THEN alias name, canonical name, config, rows/counters, and deprecation caveat SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_stream_fixture_parity_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity stream runs, THEN expected row set, projection form, orientation, score tolerance, and duplicate-edge policy SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_orientation_fixture_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity runs with incoming/outgoing orientation, THEN expected source/target id domain, row set, graph equality target, and id-map proof SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_degree_cutoff_receipt_v1` | WHEN degree cutoff is configured, THEN cutoff value, candidate nodes removed, expected rows, estimated memory delta, and measured peak delta SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_metric_config_receipt_v1` | WHEN a non-default similarity metric is configured, THEN metric name, acceptance status, scoring function, and score-tolerance oracle SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_write_mutate_fixture_parity_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity write/mutate runs, THEN relationshipsWritten, one-row invariant, graph equality or graph-store mutation, relationship type, score property, and selected materializer SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_similarity_distribution_key_receipt_v1` | WHEN any similarity distribution is requested, THEN min, max, mean, stdDev, p1, p5, p10, p25, p50, p75, p90, p95, p99, and p100 SHALL be recorded or intentionally omitted with a cap reason. |
| `profile_similarity_unique_relationship_receipt_v1` | WHEN similarity write/mutate runs with topK/topN, THEN duplicate policy, orientation, topK, topN, unique relationship count, and graph equality SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_filtered_nodesim_source_target_receipt_v1` | WHEN filtered Node Similarity runs, THEN source filter, target filter, nodesCompared, similarityPairs, relationshipsWritten, stream rows, and filter materialization SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_filtered_similarity_compute_output_split_v1` | WHEN a filter is applied, THEN the planner SHALL explain whether it reduced compute state, output materialization, or both, and compare estimated versus measured peak bytes. |

#### Compute State Is Where RAM Differentiation Lives

Pass 109 gave the memory-estimate arithmetic. Pass 110 gave the tiny fixture
parity oracle. Pass 111 connects those two to the actual compute-state
transition paths.

The spine is now:

```text
estimate receipt
  -> tiny fixture parity
  -> compute-state hook map
  -> bounded storage profile
  -> measured peak RAM / latency receipt
```

For KNN, the compute state is not "the output graph." It is an iterative
neighbor-state machine:

```text
KNN resident state:
  HugeObjectArray<NeighborList>
  per-node topK priority/value pairs
  neighborsFound counter
  joinCounter
  iteration count
  didConverge flag

KNN initialization:
  sampler.sample(...)
  compute similarity for chosen candidates
  create one NeighborList per node

KNN per-iteration temporary state:
  allOldNeighbors
  allNewNeighbors
  reverseOldNeighbors
  reverseNewNeighbors
  sampledK side state
  random joins
  neighbor-filter decisions
```

That matters because the source gives us two obvious RAM intervention points:

```text
1. Split/cursorize old/new neighbor state
   source hint: SplitOldAndNewNeighbors.apply has TODO use cursors

2. Cursorize reverse-neighbor construction
   source hint: reverseOldAndNewNeighbors has TODO cursors
```

A bounded KNN profile should therefore avoid promising "less RAM" in the
abstract. It should promise this specific trade:

```text
keep resident:
  per-node topK NeighborList
  convergence counters

make bounded/spillable:
  old/new candidate lists
  reverse old/new candidate lists
  sampled delta lists

accept:
  more passes over shards
  slower join phase
  explicit spill IO

prove:
  same candidate-generation semantics
  same updateCount behavior
  same didConverge / ranIterations surface when using GDS-compatible mode
```

KNN also has a synchronization constraint that cannot be papered over:

```text
JoinNeighbors.join:
  filter pair
  compute similarity
  fetch node1 NeighborList
  synchronized(neighbors) {
    return neighbors.add(...)
  }

NeighborList.add:
  returns INSERTED or NOT_INSERTED
  keeps topK sorted by priority
  handles equal priorities and duplicate elements
  feeds the update counter
```

So the better Rust architecture is not "just use a faster vector." It is:

```text
profile: knn_sharded_delta_profile

resident:
  NodeId -> bounded topK queue

active shard:
  old delta list
  new delta list
  reverse old list
  reverse new list

storage:
  append-only delta segments:
    node_id
    neighbor_id
    checked_state
    iteration

correctness receipt:
  candidate pairs generated
  candidate pairs filtered
  insertions accepted
  insertions rejected
  updateCount
  convergence threshold
```

For filtered KNN, the key source observation is even more product-shaped.
`FilteredKnnResult` currently retains both `targetNodeFiltering` and `KnnResult`
and chooses one producer when streaming. Its own TODO suggests splitting the two
so one can be stored and the other released.

That gives us this profile:

```text
profile: filtered_knn_single_producer_profile

preflight:
  inspect seedingSummary
  decide target-filter producer or delegate-KNN producer

retain:
  only selected producer state

release:
  unused target-filtering state or unused KNN result state

receipt:
  seededOptimally
  producerPath
  retainedBytes
  releasedBytes
  sourceFilterRows
  targetFilterRows
```

For Node Similarity, the compute-state map is different enough that sharing the
KNN profile would be a design smell.

Node Similarity prepare state:

```text
constructor:
  sourceNodes bitset
  targetNodes bitset
  sourceNodeFilter
  targetNodeFilter
  weighted flag
  sortVectors flag

prepare:
  components from provided component property, WCC, or all-same-component
  neighbor vector per node
  optional weight vector per node
  degree cutoff / upper degree cutoff
  source and target bitsets
  optional sorted target ids
```

The source also contains an important TODO:

```text
we do not need to do the rest of prepare
for a node that is not going to be used in the computation
```

That is a direct architecture lever:

```text
profile: nodesim_filter_pushed_vector_profile

before vector build:
  apply degree cutoff
  apply source/target participation checks
  apply component policy

build:
  only required neighbor vectors
  only required weight vectors
  only sorted vectors when relationship-type sort is needed

receipt:
  graphNodeCount
  sourceNodeCount
  targetNodeCount
  preparedNodeCount
  skippedNodeCount
  vectorBytes
  weightBytes
  componentBytes
```

Node Similarity candidate generation has a crucial queue ownership rule:

```text
sequential unfiltered topK:
  compare source with target ids greater than source id
  write symmetric results to topK(source) and topK(target)

filtered topK:
  iterate target ids from zero
  skip source == target
  write only the requested source/target result

parallel topK:
  compute the full non-diagonal matrix
  ensure exactly one queue handles all pairs for a single source node
  because TopKMap queues are not thread-safe
```

That means the right product profile is not just a queue implementation. It is
a queue ownership contract:

```text
profile: nodesim_queue_ownership_profile

per-source TopK queue:
  owner shard
  source id range
  target stream rule
  component id
  topK queue bytes

global TopN reducer:
  consumes TopKMap
  has separate global queue bytes
  changes fairness semantics if used alone

receipt:
  halfMatrix or fullMatrix
  filtered or unfiltered
  sequential or parallel
  source queue owner
  emitted row count
  dropped candidate count
```

Late materialization is the bridge between Neo4j-compatible surface area and
lower RAM. `NodeSimilarity.compute` already returns either a stream result or a
graph result. `computeToGraph` only uses `TopKGraph` directly for topK without
topN; otherwise it consumes a `Stream<SimilarityResult>` into
`SimilarityGraphBuilder`.

So the architecture should make this explicit:

```text
profile: similarity_late_materialization_profile

possible outputs:
  row stream
  edge-score bundle
  per-source topK graph wrapper
  materialized similarity graph

late materializer:
  internal id -> root id rewrite
  relationship type
  score property
  adjacency builder bytes
  final relationship count

receipt:
  requested mode
  stream branch or graph branch
  materialization bytes
  materialization time
  cap accepted / spilled / refused
```

The most important strategic implication:

```text
KNN and Node Similarity can share output infrastructure,
but they should not share compute storage.

Shared:
  edge-score bundle
  score distribution receipt
  write/mutate materializer
  graph equality oracle

Different:
  KNN iterative delta lists and neighbor-list insertions
  Node Similarity vector preparation and candidate matrix queues
```

Rubber duck check:

```text
If we optimize only the final src/dst/score bundle:
  KNN temp arrays can still blow the peak RAM claim.

If we spill KNN deltas but break updateCount:
  convergence and stats parity can silently drift.

If we push Node Similarity filters only after vector preparation:
  output rows may match, but the RAM differentiation is weaker.

If we use a single global TopN queue as a substitute for per-source TopK:
  memory may drop, but semantics change unless declared as a different profile.

If we materialize a similarity graph before the user asks for graph output:
  we pay adjacency bytes too early.

If we shard TopKMap without preserving single-source queue ownership:
  parallel results can become nondeterministic or unsafe.
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_knn_compute_state_transition_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN compute starts, THEN initialization strategy, max iterations, update threshold, cutoff, resident topK bytes, per-iteration update count, convergence flag, pairs considered, and selected temporary-state profile SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_delta_list_spill_receipt_v1` | WHEN KNN runs in a bounded-memory profile, THEN old/new/reverse-old/reverse-new list bytes, shard size, cursor position, spill path, replay count, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_knn_neighbor_mutation_semantics_v1` | WHEN a KNN candidate pair is joined, THEN filter decision, similarity score, queue owner, insertion result, duplicate/tie handling, perturbation rate, and convergence-counter effect SHALL be recorded or reproducibly derivable. |
| `profile_filtered_knn_release_caveat_receipt_v1` | WHEN filtered KNN selects a producer, THEN seeding summary, retained producer state, released producer state, source/target filter policy, rows emitted, and bytes avoided SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_filter_component_pushdown_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity prepares state, THEN source bitset, target bitset, degree cutoff, component policy, prepared/skipped node counts, vector bytes, weight bytes, and component bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_candidate_generation_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity generates pairs, THEN source count, target count, component id, offset rule, half/full matrix rule, filtered/unfiltered mode, and candidate-pair count SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_queue_ownership_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity uses topK in parallel, THEN source queue owner, shard/range, topK queue bytes, write isolation proof, and emitted-pair count SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_nodesim_topn_reducer_receipt_v1` | WHEN Node Similarity applies topN, THEN whether TopN consumed TopKMap or all-pairs stream, global queue bytes, topN cap, dropped rows, and semantic caveat SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_late_similarity_graph_materialization_receipt_v1` | WHEN similarity output becomes a graph, THEN stream-vs-graph branch, materializer type, id rewrite count, relationship count, score-property bytes, graph-builder bytes, and cap outcome SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_similarity_compute_output_split_receipt_v1` | WHEN an edge-score algorithm is planned, THEN compute state, durable output, API materialization, distribution calculation, and write/mutate side effects SHALL be separate byte and latency components. |

#### Starter Runtime Profiles Need Phase Receipts

Pass 108 gave WCC/PageRank/BFS memory-estimate evidence. Pass 112 connects the
PageRank/Pregel and BFS estimators to the runtime state transitions that must be
preserved by the rewrite.

The starter spine now looks like this:

```text
WCC:
  one resident DSS estimate
  -> exact component output receipt
  -> incremental/non-incremental mode receipt

PageRank:
  Pregel node-value schema
  -> messenger mode
  -> vote bits
  -> partitioned compute steps
  -> convergence/master compute
  -> score scaling
  -> stream/write/mutate materializer

BFS:
  global visited/traversed/weights/minimumChunk state
  -> task-local frontier chunks
  -> ordered chunk synchronization
  -> target/depth/no-progress termination
  -> result copy/materializer
```

For PageRank, the strongest conclusion is sober rather than flashy:

```text
The baseline GDS path is already primitive-array-heavy.

Resident:
  HugeDoubleArray for PAGE_RANK
  HugeAtomicBitSet vote bits
  HugeAtomicDoubleArray send/receive messages
  partition compute steps

Potential optimization:
  choose a cheaper messenger profile
  compress or spill message state where convergence semantics allow
  release compute/messenger state as soon as the score vector is final
  avoid extra dense materialization unless the API mode requires it

Not credible by itself:
  "Rust will make PageRank use far less RAM"
```

That means the first Rust PageRank profile should be deliberately boring:

```text
profile: pagerank_gds_compatible_pregel_profile

prove:
  same initial rank/default value policy
  same message reducer / queue mode
  same vote-to-halt semantics
  same max-iteration and tolerance behavior
  same score scaling behavior
  same estimate-row shape
```

Then we can add one differentiated profile:

```text
profile: pagerank_phase_released_message_profile

retain:
  final score array

release after convergence:
  messenger send/receive arrays
  vote bits
  compute-step state
  temporary scaler state

optional cap:
  spill message partitions
  pay extra iteration or IO time
```

For BFS, the credible differentiation is sharper because GDS already separates
fixed global state from variable local frontier state:

```text
BFS global exact state:
  visited bitset
  traversedNodes array
  weights array
  minimumChunk array
  traversal index / length atomics
  targetFoundIndex atomic

BFS task-local state:
  localNodes LongArrayList
  chunks LongArrayList
  indexOfChunk
  indexOfLocalNodes
  delta-sized work slices
```

So a bounded-RAM BFS profile should not pretend the global arrays disappear. The
product promise is narrower and more honest:

```text
profile: bfs_bounded_frontier_profile

keep exact:
  visited
  minimum predecessor
  traversal order
  target and depth semantics

bound:
  localNodes
  chunks
  result materialization

trade:
  more synchronization passes
  optional spill/replay of frontier chunks
  higher latency under tiny RAM caps
```

The phase-split receipt language is the practical bridge from research to code:

```text
For every algorithm run:
  estimate bytes before run
  allocate named resident state
  allocate named temporary state
  record phase transitions
  release temporary state
  materialize only requested API output
  compare output with GDS fixture
  compare measured peak with estimate
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_pagerank_pregel_lifecycle_receipt_v1` | WHEN PageRank runs through Pregel, THEN variant, schema keys, message mode, rank arrays, iteration count, convergence flag, and score-scaling policy SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pagerank_score_scaling_receipt_v1` | WHEN PageRank scaling is enabled, THEN scaler type, partition count, source score bytes, scaled score bytes, task count, and measured scaling latency SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pregel_partition_ownership_receipt_v1` | WHEN Pregel compute steps are created, THEN partitioning strategy, graph-copy count, compute-step count, node range or degree range, executor model, and per-thread overhead SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pregel_convergence_receipt_v1` | WHEN a Pregel iteration ends, THEN sent-message flags, vote-bit status, master-compute result, max-iteration status, and convergence reason SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pregel_node_value_schema_receipt_v1` | WHEN Pregel allocates node values, THEN schema key, value type, default initialization, backing array kind, per-node bytes, and initialization latency SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_pregel_messenger_mode_receipt_v1` | WHEN Pregel selects a messenger, THEN reducing/sync/async mode, send/receive or queue bytes, sender tracking, reset policy, and release point SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_global_state_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS starts, THEN visited, traversedNodes, weights, minimumChunk, traversal atomics, source node, target predicate, and fixed global bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_frontier_range_estimate_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS estimates memory, THEN localNodes lower/upper range, chunks estimate, delta, concurrency, relationship upper bound, and cap decision SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_local_frontier_buffer_receipt_v1` | WHEN a BFS task runs, THEN task id, claimed offsets, local-node count, chunk count, separator count, duplicate candidate count, and retained/spilled bytes SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_chunk_sync_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS synchronizes chunks, THEN currentChunkId order, visited-first append results, traversal-length delta, reset behavior, and ordering proof SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_bfs_target_depth_termination_receipt_v1` | WHEN BFS stops, THEN max-depth status, target-found index, no-progress status, termination-flag status, retained result length, and final traversal depth SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_starter_algorithm_phase_split_receipt_v1` | WHEN any starter algorithm runs, THEN resident state, temporary state, durable output, API materialization, release points, equality oracle, latency counters, and RAM-cap policy SHALL be recorded. |

Rubber duck check:

```text
If a PageRank estimate counts only final scores:
  it misses messenger arrays, vote bits, and compute steps.

If a PageRank RAM-win claim rests only on Rust:
  it ignores that GDS already uses primitive huge arrays for the hot state.

If a BFS cap hides visited/traversed/minimumChunk:
  it is not an exact BFS cap.

If a BFS cap bounds local chunks but drops chunk ordering:
  output order, target truncation, or predecessor weights can drift.

If WCC/PageRank/BFS share one generic receipt:
  the implementation will lose the exact state names that make verification easy.
```

#### WCC Is The First Exact Receipt, Not The Biggest RAM Win

Pass 113 closes the missing WCC runtime half of the starter spine. The shape is
pleasantly small:

```text
graph
  -> optional seed property
  -> HugeAtomicDisjointSetStruct
  -> strategy selector

strategy selector:
  if undirected or inverse-indexed:
    SampledStrategy
      -> sample sparse subgraph
      -> estimate largest component
      -> skip largest component where safe
      -> still link inverse relationships for correctness
  else:
    UnsampledStrategy
      -> batch offsets
      -> traverse relationships
      -> union source/target

output:
  DisjointSetStruct.asNodeProperties()
    -> setIdOf(nodeId)
```

The sober conclusion matters. WCC should be the first implementation proof loop
because it is easy to verify, not because it obviously creates a massive RAM
delta versus GDS. The baseline is already compact: a parent array, plus a seed
array only for incremental mode.

The useful WCC profiles are:

```text
profile: wcc_gds_compatible_dss_profile
  one parent array
  optional seed/community array
  exact union-by-min semantics
  exact setIdOf output

profile: wcc_streamed_edge_union_profile
  keep DSS resident
  stream relationship batches
  bound active edge traversal memory
  record union/skipped-by-threshold counts

profile: wcc_seeded_incremental_profile
  parent array
  seed/community array
  maxCommunityId side state
  proof that missing seeds receive stable new ids
```

This makes WCC valuable as the first "green path" for LLM coding:

```text
1. port estimate parity
2. port DSS state
3. port unsampled runtime
4. port sampled runtime
5. port output node properties
6. compare against GDS fixtures
7. emit one proof packet
```

New executable-spec candidates:

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `profile_wcc_strategy_selector_receipt_v1` | WHEN WCC starts, THEN graph characteristics, seed mode, threshold, batch size, selected strategy, and DSS estimate SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_unsampled_union_receipt_v1` | WHEN unsampled WCC runs, THEN offset ranges, task count, traversed edges, threshold skips, union count, and termination/progress checks SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_sampled_strategy_receipt_v1` | WHEN sampled WCC runs, THEN partition count, sampled edge cap, largest-component sampling, link-remaining phase, and inverse-link behavior SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_largest_component_skip_receipt_v1` | WHEN sampled WCC skips work for the largest component, THEN sampled component id, skipped-node count, linked-node count, and correctness-preserving inverse links SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_dss_runtime_receipt_v1` | WHEN WCC allocates DSS state, THEN parent bytes, seed bytes, node count, incremental flag, and measured peak SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_seeded_component_receipt_v1` | WHEN seeded WCC maps component ids, THEN seed property identity, max seed id, missing-seed policy, new id assignment, and output set id SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_union_semantics_receipt_v1` | WHEN WCC unions two ids, THEN roots, public set ids, union-by-min decision, CAS retries, and path-halving activity SHALL be recorded. |
| `profile_wcc_first_slice_receipt_v1` | WHEN the first starter slice is shipped, THEN WCC estimate, runtime, output parity, GDS comparison, measured RAM, latency, and exactness verdict SHALL be emitted as one proof packet. |

Rubber duck check:

```text
If we claim WCC is the big RAM breakthrough:
  that is probably an overclaim.

If we implement only unsampled WCC:
  fixture parity may pass on directed cases and fail on undirected/inverse-indexed cases.

If threshold default weight is missed:
  thresholded relationship traversal can drift.

If seeded setIdOf is treated as root id:
  incremental WCC output can drift.

If sampled WCC skips largest-component work without inverse-link correctness:
  the output can look plausible but be wrong.
```

#### Starter Slice Executable Receipt Packet

Pass 114 turns the starter evidence into an implementation-facing spec packet.
The idea is to make the first Rust slice boring, measurable, and hard to fake.

```text
starter order:
  1. WCC
     easiest exact estimate + runtime + output loop

  2. BFS
     best early RAM-cap demo because local frontier/chunks can be bounded

  3. PageRank
     best iterative-state demo, but avoid claiming easy RAM wins
```

The packet has one shared envelope and algorithm-specific receipts inside it:

```text
profile_starter_slice_executable_packet_v1
  algorithm_id
  public_mode
  fixture_id
  input_projection_manifest
  estimate_receipt
  runtime_state_receipt
  output_parity_receipt
  gds_expected_output_ref
  measured_output_ref
  measured_peak_ram_bytes
  measured_latency_ms
  exactness_verdict
```

Executable Requirements:

### REQ-STARTER-001.0: Emit One Starter-Slice Proof Packet

**WHEN** a starter algorithm fixture is executed against the Rust implementation
**THEN** the system SHALL emit one `profile_starter_slice_executable_packet_v1`
**AND** SHALL include algorithm id, public mode, fixture id, selected storage profile, GDS source commit, measured peak RAM bytes, measured latency milliseconds, and exactness verdict
**SHALL** fail closed when estimate, runtime, or output receipts are missing

### REQ-WCC-001.0: Prove WCC Estimate And Strategy Selection

**WHEN** WCC starts on a fixture graph
**THEN** the system SHALL record node count, relationship count, seed-property mode, incremental flag, threshold, graph directionality, inverse-index flag, batch size, selected sampled/unsampled strategy, and DSS estimate bytes
**AND** SHALL compare DSS estimate bytes against the GDS fixture expectation for the same node count and incremental flag
**SHALL** reject a run whose selected strategy is not derivable from graph characteristics

### REQ-WCC-002.0: Prove WCC Runtime Union Semantics

**WHEN** WCC processes relationships
**THEN** the system SHALL record sampled or unsampled phase, partition or offset range, threshold gate, union count, skipped-by-threshold count, CAS retry count, path-halving count, and final DSS parent/seed array sizes
**AND** SHALL preserve union-by-min public set id behavior and seeded component id behavior
**SHALL** fail seeded fixtures when missing seeds are returned as raw root ids instead of stable community ids

### REQ-WCC-003.0: Prove WCC Public Output Parity

**WHEN** WCC stream, stats, write, or mutate mode completes
**THEN** stream mode SHALL emit `nodeId` and `componentId` with original-id mapping and min-component-size filtering
**AND** stats/write/mutate modes SHALL emit component count, component distribution, configuration, and nonnegative timing fields matching GDS fixture shape
**AND** write/mutate modes SHALL record node properties written and target property name
**SHALL** treat component equivalence as the default invariant unless consecutive-id or seed mode requires exact ids

### REQ-BFS-001.0: Prove BFS Global And Frontier State

**WHEN** BFS starts from a source node
**THEN** the system SHALL record visited bitset bytes, traversedNodes bytes, weights bytes, minimumChunk bytes, traversal atomics, localNodes bytes, chunks bytes, delta, task count, max depth, target nodes, and termination flag status
**AND** SHALL record whether local frontier state is resident, bounded, or spill-backed
**SHALL** fail a bounded-frontier profile that omits exact visited/traversed/minimumChunk state

### REQ-BFS-002.0: Prove BFS Public Traversal Output

**WHEN** BFS stream or mutate mode completes
**THEN** stream mode SHALL emit source node, ordered node id list, and optional path using original ids
**AND** mutate mode SHALL emit relationship count, relationship type, configuration, and nonnegative timing fields
**AND** target-node, max-depth, full traversal, path, and invalid-source fixtures SHALL be verified separately
**SHALL** preserve GDS-accepted nondeterministic order families when traversal order is not fully deterministic

### REQ-PAGERANK-001.0: Prove PageRank Pregel Runtime State

**WHEN** PageRank runs through Pregel
**THEN** the system SHALL record node-value schema, rank array bytes, messenger mode, send/receive or queue bytes, vote-bit bytes, partition strategy, graph-copy count, max iterations, tolerance, convergence reason, and release points
**AND** SHALL distinguish PageRank, ArticleRank, and Eigenvector value schemas when variants are implemented
**SHALL** reject a RAM-win claim based only on Rust language/runtime without measured state-byte reduction

### REQ-PAGERANK-002.0: Prove PageRank Public Score Output

**WHEN** PageRank stream, stats, write, or mutate mode completes
**THEN** stream mode SHALL emit original `nodeId` and `score` rows within fixture tolerance
**AND** stats/write/mutate modes SHALL emit ran iterations, convergence flag, centrality distribution presence, configuration, node properties written where applicable, and nonnegative timing fields
**AND** weighted, unweighted, source-node, invalid-weight-property, write-back, and mutate fixtures SHALL be distinct tests
**SHALL** fail if final score scaling or original-id rewriting changes public scores

#### WCC First Fixture And Projection Bridge

Pass 116 fills the missing "first runnable fixture" gap.
The starter implementation prompt now has a concrete tiny graph oracle and a
local projection mechanism to use before any large benchmark.

GDS WCC ten-node oracle:

```text
nodes:
  nA Label  nodeId=0 seedId=42
  nB Label  nodeId=1 seedId=42
  nC Label  nodeId=2 seedId=42
  nD Label  nodeId=3 seedId=42
  nE Label2 nodeId=4
  nF Label2 nodeId=5
  nG Label2 nodeId=6
  nH Label2 nodeId=7
  nI Label2 nodeId=8
  nJ Label2 nodeId=9

relationships:
  nA -TYPE-> nB
  nB -TYPE-> nC
  nC -TYPE-> nD
  nD -TYPE {cost: 4.2}-> nE
  nE -TYPE-> nF
  nF -TYPE-> nG
  nH -TYPE-> nI

default WCC expected equivalence:
  component 1: nA, nB, nC, nD, nE, nF, nG
  component 2: nH, nI
  component 3: nJ
```

Why this is the right first fixture:

| Fixture property | What it proves |
|---|---|
| Ten nodes | Small enough for exact hand inspection and stable JSON receipts. |
| Three components | Forces component grouping, isolated-node handling, and distribution output. |
| Mixed labels | Allows label-filter tests without changing topology. |
| Seed ids on `nA`-`nD` | Gives a path to seeded/incremental WCC after default mode passes. |
| One `cost: 4.2` edge | Gives a threshold-sensitive split case after default mode passes. |
| Natural projection | Matches the GDS fixture's first projection mode. |

Local projection bridge:

```text
GraphProjectionMetadata
  owner_user
  database_name
  snapshot_generation
  node_count
  relationship_count
  memory_estimate
  node_property_rows
  relationship_property_rows

GraphProjectionCatalog.project
  spec + metadata -> GraphProjectionHandle

GraphProjectionCatalog.stream_node_properties
  projected rows -> sorted nodeId/property rows
```

Local memory envelope already exists:

```text
MemoryEstimate.new(
  topology_reference_bytes,
  duplicate_topology_bytes,
  sidecar_bytes,
  catalog_metadata_bytes,
  heap_bytes,
  page_cache_bytes,
  direct_io_buffer_bytes,
  algorithm_state_bytes,
  delta_overlay_bytes,
  scratch_bytes
)

MemoryEstimate.projection(...)
  sets duplicate topology, direct IO, algorithm state, delta overlay, and scratch to zero
```

That means WCC estimate v1 should add algorithm-state bytes without mutating the
projection estimate meaning. The first receipt can compare:

```text
projection bytes:
  topology_reference_bytes
  sidecar_bytes
  catalog_metadata_bytes
  heap_bytes
  page_cache_bytes

WCC algorithm bytes:
  dss_parent_bytes
  dss_seed_bytes
  output_materialization_bytes
  receipt_bytes
  scratch_bytes
```

| Candidate | Contract |
|---|---|
| `fixture_wcc_neo4j_ten_node_oracle_v1` | WHEN creating the first WCC fixture, THEN the local fixture SHALL represent the ten GDS nodes, seven `TYPE` relationships, labels, `nodeId`, `seedId`, `cost`, expected components, and isolated-node behavior. |
| `profile_wcc_fixture_projection_manifest_v1` | WHEN the fixture is projected, THEN the receipt SHALL record graph name, node count, relationship count, orientation, labels, relationship type, seed property availability, threshold property availability, memory estimate, and property-plane rows. |
| `fixture_wcc_public_mode_matrix_v1` | WHEN WCC public modes are tested, THEN stream, stats, write, and mutate expectations SHALL be represented as distinct mode rows with output keys, component count, distribution, properties written, timings, and equality oracle. |

first green path:
  1. encode fixture_wcc_neo4j_ten_node_oracle_v1
  2. project it through the existing local catalog shape
  3. run WCC default stream mode
  4. emit component-equivalence output receipt
